subject: social_science

concepts.title: Grant of Diwani to the East India Company
concepts.definition: The official authorization granted by the Mughal Emperor in August 1765 designating the East India Company as the chief financial administrator of Bengal.
concepts.key_idea: Transformed a foreign trading enterprise into the sovereign revenue administrator of Bengal.
question_patterns: explain the significance of the grant of Diwani to the East India Company in 1765
how did the appointment as Diwan change the functioning of the East India Company
what role did Robert Clive play during the grant of Diwani
describe how becoming Diwan affected British administration in Bengal
why was obtaining the Diwani considered a major milestone for the British

solution_steps.action: identify the date and authority of appointment
solution_steps.explain: the Mughal emperor appointed the Company as Diwan on 12 August 1765
the Company became chief financial administrator, allowing local revenues to finance colonial trade

concepts.title: Bengal Revenue Crisis and Famine of 1770
concepts.definition: An economic downturn in Bengal caused by relentless revenue extraction by the British, resulting in severe rural distress and a famine in 1770 that wiped out one-third of the population.
concepts.key_idea: Excessive revenue extraction without financial investment ruined the agrarian economy.
question_patterns: describe the economic crisis in Bengal following the grant of Diwani
what were the primary causes and consequences of the Bengal famine of 1770
how did colonial trade policies impoverish peasants and artisans in Bengal
explain why artisanal production and agriculture declined rapidly after 1765
examine how forced sales at low prices affected Bengal producers

solution_steps.explain: artisans were compelled to sell goods cheaply while peasants faced excessive tax demands
the 1770 famine killed ten million people, causing widespread rural economic collapse

concepts.title: Permanent Settlement of 1793
concepts.definition: A land revenue system introduced by Governor-General Lord Cornwallis in 1793 in which revenue rates were fixed permanently and local elites were made hereditary zamindars.
concepts.key_idea: Fixed revenue demands permanently to guarantee steady income and encourage private investment in land.
question_patterns: what were the main features of the Permanent Settlement introduced in 1793
who introduced the Permanent Settlement system in Bengal
why did the British fix land revenue permanently under Cornwallis
describe the role assigned to zamindars under the Permanent Settlement
explain how the British expected Permanent Settlement to encourage agricultural investment

solution_steps.explain: introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793, recognizing rajas and taluqdars as zamindars
revenue demand was permanently fixed so zamindars could retain surplus from land improvements

concepts.title: Problems of the Permanent Settlement
concepts.definition: Flaws in the Permanent Settlement where high revenue demands caused zamindars to forfeit estates while peasants suffered under oppressive rents and insecure tenure.
concepts.key_idea: Immoderately high initial rates ruined zamindars and deprived cultivators of land security.
question_patterns: what problems arose from the implementation of the Permanent Settlement
why did many zamindars lose their estates under the Permanent Settlement
how did the Permanent Settlement oppress actual cultivators in Bengal villages
explain why zamindars failed to invest in improving agricultural land
describe the condition of under-tenants as noted by Colebrook

solution_steps.explain: initial revenue rates were set so high that failing zamindars had their estates auctioned
cultivators faced high rents, debt burdens, and risk of eviction by intermediaries

concepts.title: Mahalwari Settlement System
concepts.definition: A land revenue framework created by Holt Mackenzie in 1822 for North Western Provinces, assessing revenue village-by-village (mahal) with periodic revisions.
concepts.key_idea: Assessed revenue per village collective with periodic revisions under village headmen control.
question_patterns: explain the working of the Mahalwari system devised by Holt Mackenzie
how was the Mahalwari system different from the Permanent Settlement
what was a mahal in British revenue records
who was responsible for collecting revenue in the Mahalwari system
why did the British periodically revise revenue demands under the Mahalwari system

solution_steps.explain: revenue was calculated by surveying individual plots within a village estate or mahal
village headmen collected and remitted revised revenue directly to the government

concepts.title: Ryotwari System (Munro System)
concepts.definition: A direct revenue arrangement devised by Alexander Read and Thomas Munro in southern India, settling tax assessments directly with individual agricultural cultivators (ryots).
concepts.key_idea: Direct settlement with individual farmers without intermediary zamindars.
question_patterns: describe the features of the Ryotwari or Munro system in South India
why were zamindars bypassed in the southern revenue settlement
what role did Thomas Munro play in shaping South Indian revenue collection
how were land surveys conducted prior to Ryotwari revenue assessments
explain why revenue demand in the Ryotwari system led to desertion of villages

solution_steps.explain: developed by Read and Munro in Madras presidency without traditional zamindars
cultivators fields were surveyed individually to fix revenue demands directly

concepts.title: Plough Requirement Calculation for Indigo Cultivation
concepts.definition: The calculation of total agricultural ploughs required for a given area of land under nij indigo cultivation, where each bigha requires exactly two ploughs.
concepts.key_idea: Every bigha under indigo requires two ploughs for cultivation.
question_patterns: calculate the number of ploughs required for a given number of bighas of indigo cultivation
how many ploughs are needed to cultivate indigo on a specified bigha plot
find the total ploughs required for an indigo planter with a given land area in bighas
determine the number of ploughs necessary for cultivating indigo over a bigha area
compute the required ploughs for a specified bigha landholding in Bengal

solution_steps.explain: each bigha of indigo land requires two ploughs for proper preparation

concepts.title: Nij and Ryoti Systems of Indigo Cultivation
concepts.definition: The two primary modes of commercial indigo production: nij, where planters cultivated directly controlled lands, and ryoti, where ryots were bound by cash advances to grow indigo.
concepts.key_idea: Planters produced indigo either on direct estates or through forced peasant debt contracts.
question_patterns: differentiate between nij and ryoti systems of indigo cultivation
what problems did planters face under the nij system of indigo cultivation
how did the contract or satta system operate under ryoti cultivation
why were peasants reluctant to grow indigo under the ryoti system
explain how cash advances trapped ryots in a continuous cycle of debt

solution_steps.explain: nij involved direct planter ownership while ryoti forced peasants to dedicate land via contracts
nij suffered from shortage of compact land and ploughs, while ryoti trapped peasants in debt

concepts.title: Indigo Processing in Vats
concepts.definition: The multi-stage chemical extraction of indigo dye in factory vats involving plant fermentation, paddle beating with lime water, and sediment molding.
concepts.key_idea: Sequential vat fermentation, oxidation beating, and pressing transformed green leaves into blue dye.
question_patterns: describe the step by step process of manufacturing indigo dye in vats
what were the functions of the steeper vat and beater vat in indigo manufacturing
how was lime water utilized during the indigo dye production process
explain the role of vat beaters in extracting indigo dye
what happened to the indigo solution after beating was completed

solution_steps.explain: indigo leaves were soaked in warm water in the steeper vat until fermented
liquid was stirred in beater vat with lime water, settling sediment into blue pulp for pressing

concepts.title: The Blue Rebellion and Indigo Commission
concepts.definition: The massive agrarian uprising of Bengal ryots in 1859 against indigo planters, leading to the 1860 Indigo Commission report that condemned planter coercion.
concepts.key_idea: Peasant uprising in Bengal ended forced indigo cultivation and led to official reform.
question_patterns: what were the causes and consequences of the Blue Rebellion of 1859
how did women and local headmen participate in the Indigo Rebellion
what were the findings and recommendations of the Indigo Commission of 1860
why did indigo production collapse in Bengal and shift to Bihar
how was Mahatma Gandhi associated with the indigo planters in Champaran

solution_steps.explain: ryots refused advances, attacked factories, and boycotted planters due to harsh exploitation
Indigo Commission declared production unprofitable for ryots, allowing them to refuse future sowing
